title: CHF Clinical Evidence Blueprint v1
description: Extension-only manifest. Does NOT create a new disease, new NYHA classes, or new PPS/KPS/ADL support concepts -- 'Congestive Heart Failure' under the Cardiovascular System / 'Heart Failure and Advanced Cardiac Disease' family already exists (PR #38, merged) with its own self-contained NYHA Class I-IV variants and KPS/PPS/ADL HOSPICE_ELIGIBILITY_SUPPORT concepts. This manifest adds only what PR #38 does not already contain: (1) a small set of missing atomic CHF concepts (Orthopnea, Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea, Refractory Symptoms Despite Optimal Treatment, Cardiac Cachexia, Treatment Resistant Congestive Heart Failure, Increasing Care Needs) with provenance metadata; (2) three cross-disease OntologyRelationship edges linking CHF's existing NYHA Class IV / PPS Less Than 70 Percent / KPS Less Than 70 Percent concepts to the corresponding Functional Assessment Framework v1 (PR #49, merged) scale-definition concepts, so a nurse viewing CHF evidence can navigate to the full scale interpretation without any assessment definition ever being duplicated; (3) a recertification evidence trend model (8 PROGNOSTIC_INDICATOR concepts covering NYHA/PPS/KPS/ADL/weight/hospitalization/symptom/narrative trend) for CHF; (4) a documentation-only AI capability boundary (ai_may / ai_may_not), mirroring the pattern already established in the Functional Assessment Framework v1 manifest's trend_policy. No schema, migration, or API changes. No existing PR #38 or PR #49 row is ever modified, renamed, or duplicated.

scope.family: Heart Failure and Advanced Cardiac Disease

new_concepts.name: Orthopnea
new_concepts.description: Dyspnea that occurs or worsens when lying flat and is relieved by sitting or standing upright, reflecting rising left-sided filling pressures in decompensated heart failure.

new_concepts.name: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea
new_concepts.description: Sudden episodes of severe shortness of breath and coughing that awaken the patient from sleep, typically requiring the patient to sit up or stand for relief; a marker of worsening heart failure.

new_concepts.name: Refractory Symptoms Despite Optimal Treatment
new_concepts.description: Persistent or recurrent heart failure symptoms (dyspnea, edema, fatigue) that continue despite optimized guideline-directed medical therapy, diuretics, and other disease-directed treatment.

new_concepts.name: Cardiac Cachexia
new_concepts.description: Unintentional, progressive loss of lean body mass and weight in the setting of advanced heart failure, reflecting a systemic catabolic state associated with poor prognosis.

new_concepts.name: Treatment Resistant Congestive Heart Failure
new_concepts.description: Heart failure symptoms and functional decline that persist or progress despite optimally dosed, guideline-directed medical therapy and device/procedural interventions where clinically appropriate.

new_concepts.name: Increasing Care Needs
new_concepts.description: A pattern of escalating reliance on caregivers or paid care for activities of daily living and household tasks, reflecting progressive functional decline in advanced heart failure.

new_concepts.name: COPD
new_concepts.description: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease as a co-morbid condition alongside Congestive Heart Failure; overlapping dyspnea and functional decline should be evaluated in the complete clinical picture.

new_concepts.name: Stroke
new_concepts.description: Prior cerebrovascular accident (stroke) as a co-morbid condition alongside Congestive Heart Failure; may compound functional decline and ADL dependence.

new_concepts.name: Cancer
new_concepts.description: Concurrent malignancy as a co-morbid condition alongside Congestive Heart Failure; relevant to overall prognosis review and the complete clinical picture.

new_concepts.name: ALS
new_concepts.description: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) as a co-morbid condition alongside Congestive Heart Failure; compounding neuromuscular and functional decline relevant to the complete clinical picture.

functional_assessment_linkage.faf_concept_name: NYHA - New York Heart Association Functional Classification
functional_assessment_linkage.description: Links CHF's existing NYHA Class IV finding to the Functional Assessment Framework's NYHA scale definition for full nurse-facing score interpretation, without duplicating the scale's level content.

Links CHF's existing PPS Less Than 70 Percent hospice-eligibility-support concept to the Functional Assessment Framework's PPS scale definition for full nurse-facing score interpretation, without duplicating the scale's level content.

Links CHF's existing KPS Less Than 70 Percent hospice-eligibility-support concept to the Functional Assessment Framework's KPS scale definition for full nurse-facing score interpretation, without duplicating the scale's level content.

trend_indicators.name: NYHA Classification Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's previous NYHA class to the current NYHA class at recertification; a worsening class supports continued functional-decline documentation.

trend_indicators.name: PPS Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's previous PPS score to the current PPS score at recertification; a decreasing score supports continued functional-decline documentation.

trend_indicators.name: KPS Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's previous KPS score to the current KPS score at recertification; a decreasing score supports continued functional-decline documentation.

trend_indicators.name: ADL Status Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's previous ADL dependence status to the current status at recertification; increasing dependence supports continued functional-decline documentation.

trend_indicators.name: Weight Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's weight between the previous and current certification periods, documenting unintentional weight loss.

trend_indicators.name: Hospitalization Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of hospitalization or emergency-treatment frequency between the previous and current certification periods, documenting an increasing pattern.

trend_indicators.name: Symptom Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of symptom burden (dyspnea, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, edema) between the previous and current certification periods.

trend_indicators.name: Narrative Trend
trend_indicators.description: A structured narrative summary comparing the patient's overall clinical course between the previous and current certification periods, supporting the physician's recertification determination.

differentiation_guards: This manifest never creates a new OntologyDisease, OntologyDiseaseFamily, or OntologyBodySystem row -- it resolves the existing Congestive Heart Failure disease and the existing Functional Assessment Framework disease by exact name and aborts if either is missing.
This manifest never creates a new OntologyDiseaseVariant row (no new NYHA classes, no new severity tiers).
This manifest never creates a duplicate NYHA/PPS/KPS/ADL definition -- it links to PR #38's and PR #49's existing rows via OntologyRelationship only.

Functional assessments and CHF clinical evidence support functional status documentation, clinical decline documentation, recertification review, and clinical picture development; they do not independently establish diagnosis, prognosis, hospice eligibility, or terminal status.
